title: Cell-based Therapy for Heart Failure in Rat: Double Thoracotomy for Myocardial Infarction and Epicardial Implantation of Cells and Biomatrix
protocol: Anesthetize the rats with isoflurane 5% and O₂ 5 L/min in an induction chamber for 5 min.
Place the animal’s snout into a nose cone connected to the anesthesia system.
Perform a toe or tail pinch to confirm sedation.
Remove the skin from the leg with scissors by cutting the skin from ankle to the hip.
Remove the muscles and cut the femoral artery for animal exsanguination.
Expose the hip joint and dislocate the femur head without damaging it.
Place the bones in sterile PBS in a 50 ml plastic tube.
Remove all muscles and ligaments from the bones without breaking them.
Rinse the peeled bones in 70% ethanol for 5 min.
Cut both tips of the bones with scissors under sterile laminar flow hood conditions.
Flush the bone marrow by injecting sterile PBS into the bone extremity.
Collect marrow into a 15 ml tube.
Centrifuge the collected marrow at 300 x g for 7 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Suspend the pellet in 3 ml of Red Blood Cell Lysis buffer.
Incubate the suspension for 1 min at room temperature.
Spin again for 7 min at 300 x g.
In a 150 ml culture flask, add sterile cell culture medium (395 ml IMDM medium, 5 ml pen/strep, 100 ml FBS).
Seed the cells.
Change the medium on the second day to remove nonadherent cells.
Perform medium changes every second day for 2-3 weeks until desired cell quantity is obtained.
Alternatively, prepare the biograft by seeding the cells onto the solid matrix as needed.
On the day of cardiac implantation, prepare the cells or harvest the biograft just before epicardial application.
Collect the cells using Accutase cell detachment solution.
Count the cells.
Fill a 1.5 ml centrifuge tube with the volume of cell suspension calculated to obtain desired cell quantity.
Centrifuge for 7 min at 300 x g.
Remove the supernatant.
Alternatively, harvest the biograft from cell culture medium.
Rinse in sterile PBS.
Keep the biograft in fresh culture medium without serum.
Weigh the rat.
Turn on the heating pad at 37 °C.
Anesthetize the rat with 5% isoflurane and 5 L/min 100% O2 in an induction chamber for 5-7 min.
Perform a toe or tail pinch to confirm sedation.
Place the rat on the heating pad.
Intubate the animal with a 14 G i.v. catheter.
Connect the intubation catheter to a rodent ventilator programmed for settings including 2.5 L/min oxygen, 2.5% isoflurane, tidal volume of 2 ml, and breathing frequency of 90 breaths/min.
Prepare a buprenorphine solution at 0.1 mg/kg.
Inject subcutaneously one third of the prepared buprenorphine solution.
Shave the left part of the thorax.
Disinfect with a 1% Betadine solution.
Incise the skin perpendicular to the sternum at the fourth intercostal space.
Separate the three layers of thoracic muscle (pectoralis major, ascending pectoralis, and external oblique pectoralis).
Open the fourth intercostal space (between ribs 4 and 5).
Use a small retractor to spread the ribs and expose the heart.
Open the pericardium carefully.
Locate and ligate the left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) with a 7.0 suture, placing it 4 mm below the atrium.
Close the intercostal space with two stitches using 3.0 sutures.
Position the two sutures proximally and distally from the sternum.
First, tighten the distal suture.
Clamp the ventilator exhaust tubing for 2 sec to inflate the chest and avoid pneumothorax.
Tighten the second suture.
Position the muscle layers back in place without additional sutures.
Close the skin with a 5.0 suture.
Disinfect the suture with a 1% Betadine solution.
Inject the remaining buprenorphine solution.
Turn off the anesthesia system.
Remove intubation catheter.
Keep the rat in the cage under a warm lamp for 1-2 hours.
Monitor the temperature inside the cage to avoid overheating.
Return the rat to the IVC unit after warming.
Inject subcutaneously Buprenorphine at 0.05-0.1 mg/kg post-operatively every 6-12 hours for 48 hours.
Incise the skin perpendicular to the sternum at the fifth intercostal space.
Separate the pectoralis major, ascending pectoralis, and external oblique pectoralis muscles.
Open the fifth intercostal space between ribs 5 and 6.
Use a small retractor to spread the ribs and expose the heart.
Carefully remove any adherence with fine forceps if present.
Locate the infarct area which appears as a pale region below the ligature.
Insert a 10 cm piece of suture (7.0) at the apex when necessary for better visualization.
Pull gently on the suture maintained loosely by a clamp to expose the heart.
Position the biograft at the surface of the heart.
Prewarm the prefilled fibrin sealant syringe at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Apply a drop (50-100 μl) of fibrin sealant under the biograft using a 25 G Luer needle.
Verify that the biograft is perfectly sealed.
Apply the cell pellet collected onto the pale area below the ligature using a pipette tip.
Apply a drop (50-100 μl) of fibrin sealant onto the applied cell pellet.
